uncited: This family covers the initialization strategies and iterative optimization procedures required to reconstruct 3D scenes from 2D images using 3D Gaussian Splatting [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md].
It solves the problem of converting sparse or dense image collections into a set of differentiable volumetric primitives that can be rendered in real time [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md].

It differs from implicit neural field methods by optimizing explicit, static or dynamic ellipsoids via differentiable rasterization, achieving faster convergence and rendering speeds [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md].
All methods in this family optimize a set of $N$ 3D Gaussian primitives [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md].
The optimization minimizes a loss function $\mathcal{L}$ between rendered images and ground truth views, typically using the Adam optimizer [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md].
The rendering process involves projecting 3D Gaussians to 2D screen space, sorting by depth, and alpha blending [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md].
3D Gaussian Splatting was introduced by Kerbl et al. in 2023 [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md].
The initialization policy using power-law opacity scaling was detailed in [1398-3dgs-initialization-policy.md].
GauFRe was proposed to address optimization instability in dynamic scenes by separating static and dynamic components [7994-gaufre.md].
